summary:
Held 1 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 5 upside misses — G1A.DE +6%, EDV.L +5%, III.L +5%, AAL.L +5%, AAF.L +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (AD.AS -7%, BESI.AS -6%, IFX.DE -6%, CBK.DE -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: AD.AS (-6.71%) — Read-through selloff after Albertsons slashed FY26 sales/EPS guidance on weak US grocery spending (stock -24% on 7/23); AD.AS gets ~60% of sales from US banners (Stop & Shop, Giant, Food Lion, Hannaford), hit ahead of its Aug 5 Q2 report. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — AD.AS is a Euronext Amsterdam consumer-staples/grocery name; uk-eu momentum/growth universes are typically screened from tech/industrial/high-beta names and structurally exclude defensive retailers like this.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings beat: 1.9% organic revenue growth and improved YoY operating profit vs. estimates, plus commentary that June momentum carried into July.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — RAND.AS is a Euronext Amsterdam-listed staffing/HR services mid-cap with no US ADR, so it never entered a US-centric equity screen; also an overnight earnings gap that pre-market/EU-session positioning would capture, not a US post-open signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an EU/Euronext large-cap sleeve (e.g. AEX constituents) to the universe with an earnings-gap release rule (gap ≥8% on reported-day open) so foreign-listed gainers like RAND.AS become eligible.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 beat: orders/revenue ~5% above consensus, EBITDA +7%; GEA raised FY26 guidance (organic growth to 6-8%, EBITDA margin to 17.0-17.4%), driving the ~5.6% jump.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GEA (G1A.DE) is a German DAX industrial/food-processing equipment maker not on the uk-eu coverage list, so no filter ever saw today's earnings gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend uk-eu universe to include DAX constituents (or any EU industrial ≥€5B market cap) and add an earnings-gate that releases names gapping ≥5% on above-average post-print volume.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news; sector-wide gold miner rally as safe-haven gold demand rose ~1.5% on escalating US-Iran/Middle East tensions, lifting Endeavour Mining alongside Newmont, Barrick, Gold Fields, Sibanye.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Endeavour Mining is a West Africa-focused gold miner (Mali/Burkina Faso/Senegal/Ivory Coast operations), a commodity/mining-sector mid-cap the bot's uk-eu universe likely excludes on sector or jurisdiction-risk grounds rather than liquidity.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a gold-miner sleeve (e.g. EDV.L, GDX-equivalent LSE constituents) to the uk-eu universe with a gold-spot-correlation trigger, so sector-wide bullion rallies driven by safe-haven flows get captured, not just single-name earnings movers.

top_movers.catalyst: 3i's 23-Jul Q1 update showed NAV/share up to 3,131p (from 3,030p) and top holding Action posting H1 net sales +14%, EBITDA +13%, easing prior growth-slowdown fears.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — 3i is a closed-end PE/investment-trust holding company (NAV-driven, not an operating business), a category typically screened out of momentum/mean-reversion universes built for standard equities.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a scheduled-RNS gate for large-cap UK investment trusts/PE holdcos that flags names with NAV-update-day gaps ≥3%, instead of blanket-excluding the NAV-vehicle category.

top_movers.catalyst: Anglo American cut 2026 copper cash-cost guidance to ~145c/lb from 172c/lb (Peru to 65c from 100c) on by-product credits; Teck merger reaffirmed on track for Sep2026-Mar2027 close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AAL.L is a large-cap FTSE100 diversified miner/commodity name, a sector the uk-eu strategies likely don't screen at all, so no filter ever got the chance to evaluate it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a metals/mining sub-universe (FTSE 100 miners: AAL.L, GLEN.L, RIO.L, ANTO.L) to the uk-eu screen with a cost-guidance-revision event trigger, since these names move hard on cash-cost updates, not price action.

top_movers.catalyst: No single dated news event; likely driven by continued $110M buyback execution and speculation ahead of the Jul 31, 2026 Airtel Money listing deadline / $515M buyback trigger.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AAF.L is LSE/FTSE 100-listed but its revenue geography (Nigeria, East & Francophone Africa) likely gets it tagged as African EM by country-exposure filters, so uk-eu universe screens built on revenue geography rather than listing exchange exclude it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an LSE-listing-exchange override so FTSE 100 constituents like AAF.L qualify for the uk-eu universe regardless of revenue-geography EM tagging.

top_movers.catalyst: Read-through selloff after Albertsons slashed FY26 sales/EPS guidance on weak US grocery spending (stock -24% on 7/23); AD.AS gets ~60% of sales from US banners (Stop & Shop, Giant, Food Lion, Hannaford), hit ahead of its Aug 5 Q2 report.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AD.AS is a Euronext Amsterdam consumer-staples/grocery name; uk-eu momentum/growth universes are typically screened from tech/industrial/high-beta names and structurally exclude defensive retailers like this.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a cross-market peer-contagion scanner: when a US sector peer (e.g. Albertsons/Kroger) posts a guidance-cut move beyond a -15% threshold, pull EU/UK names with >30% revenue exposure to that sector onto a watchlist regardless of the core universe filter.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2-26 revenue/orders beat (record €292.9M orders, +128.8% YoY) but Q3 gross-margin guidance (63-65%) fell below Q2's 65.7% actual, spooking investors on cycle-peak fears.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — Besi is a Euronext Amsterdam semicap-equipment name (AI/photonics supplier), likely excluded as non-US/non-core-index and only ADR-traded (BESIY) domestically.
top_movers.suggestion: Add Euronext AEX semicap/AI-supply-chain names (incl. BESI.AS) to the uk-eu universe and add an earnings-day gate flagging post-results gaps ≥5% for next-day review even for non-covered tickers.

top_movers.catalyst: No IFX-specific news; European chip-sector selloff spilling over from STMicroelectronics' automotive/industrial earnings miss (-15% on 7/23), dragging peer semis incl. IFX lower.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — IFX.DE is a XETRA-listed large-cap (DAX) European semiconductor; bot's uk-eu strategies likely scope to US-listed/ADR names or exclude Frankfurt-primary-listed industrials, so a sector read-across move had no strategy positioned to react.
top_movers.suggestion: Extend the uk-eu momentum/news-reactive universe to include DAX-listed semiconductor names (or the IFNNY ADR) above a $30M ADV floor so sector-contagion selloffs like the STM-driven chip rout get flagged next time.

top_movers.catalyst: Commerzbank chairman said the board will open takeover talks with UniCredit but rejected any Berlin-brokered shortcut; shares fell toward/below the implied 0.485-ratio offer value (~€37.30) as merger-arb uncertainty resurfaced.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CBK.DE is a DAX financial embroiled in a binary, politically-entangled M&A/takeover situation, a category momentum and mean-reversion universes typically exclude since price action tracks deal terms/regulatory headlines, not technical signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a small event-driven/merger-arb sleeve for names under active tender offers, triggered on deal-keyword news ("takeover talks", "exchange ratio") and sized to spread-vs-offer-price rather than the standard technical filter stack.
